claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the Pulumi docs support section's provider support policy page).
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Pulumi provides long-term security updates for some providers (the policy identifies which providers get long-term security updates).
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists and lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry at /registry/ shows the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes during an update on error; it completes pending in-progress operations, then exits and reports the error.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for automated drift detection and remediation on a schedule; pulumi up --refresh refreshes and applies in a single step.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine; some Pulumi providers use Terraform schemas, while native providers map directly to cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic for upgrading from the immediately previous major version.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving long-term support updates are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Registry package pages exist at /registry/packages/ for aws, azure, azure-native, azuread, command, docker-build, gcp, kubernetes, tls, and vault.

The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs in the provider's code or direct dependencies and fixes for broken internal infrastructure needed to ship them.

A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS providers are compatible with the version of Pulumi they were frozen at unless otherwise prompted via security fixes.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.
When N+1 ships, it becomes the new N, the old N becomes the new LTS major, and the old LTS major reaches end of life the same day regardless of remaining 12-month window.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
LTS provider releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version (recommended) automatically receive patch releases as they ship.
Older majors than the LTS version receive no patches; if v3 is newest, v2 is N-1 and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
End-of-life versions (N-2 and older) are not supported and receive no updates.
